# Campaign: {{campaign.name}}

This folder is a Yllir campaign. The master is the person you talk to; they may never have used an AI or a terminal.

## Entry point

For every message from the master, first invoke the skill `yllir:yllir`. It recognises what the master wants and runs the right process. Do not answer, write or change anything before it.

## Language

Everything the master reads (messages, documents, saved-version sentences) is in the language with ISO code `{{language.main}}`. Prose register for narrative descriptions: `{{prose.register}}`.

Framework files and these instructions are in English. Do not translate them.

## Plugin root

Yllir plugin root: {{plugin.root}}. Wherever a skill or agent file mentions `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, use this path if the variable is empty.

## Words the master sees

Use only the master-facing words listed in the lexicon of the `yllir` skill. Never say: skill, script, git, commit, repository, YAML, frontmatter, metadata block, sub-agent, model, hook, MCP, template.

## Writing

The main assistant writes campaign documents only through the engine command, one batch per commit. Read `{{plugin.root}}/skills/core/yllir/authoring.md` once per conversation, before the first process or the first question about the world, and follow it.

## Fixed rules

These rules cannot be changed by settings or by the master's rules.

- Write campaign documents only through the engine, as `authoring.md` describes; never write a campaign document directly.
- A named character defined in a plot document needs their own character sheet. The sheet is the source of truth for who the character is, never for what the character does in the plot. Create sheets only through the processes.
- Canonical documents are organized by category first and geography second. Put a subject at the common ancestor of its current `location` and its explicit scene `appearances`; use the campaign-language equivalent of `Da collocare` when no location is established. A scene records `appearances` as a block list, one item per subject (`- subject: ID` with `location: [PLACE_ID]` indented under it; the flow form `[{...}]` is rejected), only when its text explicitly establishes the presence. Never infer presence from `characters`, `items`, links, names or mentions. Session scene files remain the originals; geographic views are symbolic links to them.
- A significant item named or used in a plot document gets its own item sheet when it has notable value, effects, secrets, or a plot role. Ordinary scenery and incidental props do not. Item sheets describe what the item is, never its chronology. Plot events may declare relevant item ids as `items: [id]` metadata.
- Item sheets keep the public `In breve`/`In brief`, `Description`, and `Effects` sections separate from the final master-only block. The public sections describe the item only as the players know it: what they see, what was said or identified at the table, what anyone in the world would know. They never state or hint at what the players do not know (hidden nature, curses, unidentified effects, true origin). The brief concisely describes visible appearance and known essential function; the full description adds known context when available instead of merely repeating the brief. Effects lists only the effects known to the players. The master-only block holds the full context of the item, not only its secrets: what it really is, its true origin, its complete real effects, its plot uses, and what the players do not know yet. A short card description uses `In breve`/`In brief` when present and falls back to `Description` for legacy sheets. Public extracts never include the master-only block.
- After any change to a campaign document, its mentions must be linked. The engine adds the links at each commit; never type link syntax by hand.
- Every commit reviews the complete geographic layout plan before any campaign mutation, then applies it before linking. Downstream checks use the final canonical paths.
- Without git the framework writes nothing: tell the master that the campaign needs git, and write nothing.
- The block between `<!-- master -->` and `<!-- /master -->` holds the master's private notes. Never copy it into anything meant for players, image services, web searches or publishing.
- Never delete or rewrite history. Going back is always a new saved version.
- Blocks such as `AUDIT REPORT` are results for the skill that invoked the one producing them, never messages for the master: never end your turn with one; continue the invoking skill. Your turn ends only with a message to the master, in the campaign language, using the master's words.
